data.name: Sthir
data.gender_notes: Sthir is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'sthira', meaning 'to be firm, steadfast, unwavering, or stable'. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is also known as Sthira-Bhuta-Prasada-Rupa, which translates to 'one who is pleased with the firmness of the earth'. The name Sthir carries the meaning “Firm, steadfast, unwavering” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Sthir usually hope their child will grow to embody firm, steadfast, unwavering and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner strength and stability, helping one to weather life's storms and remain grounded in their beliefs.

In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is seen as the embodiment of stability, and the name Sthir is believed to bring one closer to the divine consciousness represented by the Lord. Moreover, it is likely that a person named Sthir would strive to embody the virtues of stability and steadfastness in their daily life, bringing them closer to their higher self and the ultimate goal of spiritual enlightenment.
